- **Native Go subcommand** — reimplement as `entire hooks claude-code statusline` (no Node dependency,
  single binary, reuses the CLI's internal trail/auth/git logic instead of a subprocess).
- **Opt-in, never clobber** — only installed via an explicit flag/prompt; if the user already has a
  `statusLine` configured, skip and warn instead of overwriting.
- **Claude Code only** — Pi already shows the trail link via its extension footer; no other agent has a
  `settings.json` status-line mechanism. No generic interface yet.

The native command must replicate the `.mjs`'s perf-critical shape: every poll does only fast,
in-process, **local** work (go-git branch/remote lookup + cache read) and serves the cached result;
the slow authenticated API lookup runs in a **detached background refresh** that rewrites the cache.

Done. Here's what I built and verified.

## Summary

The Entire trail status line is now a native CLI feature for Claude Code — no Node dependency, opt-in, and never clobbers a user's existing status line.

### What was added

**`entire hooks claude-code statusline`** (`cmd/entire/cli/claude_statusline.go`) — a native Go port of the `.mjs` script:
- **Serve mode** (every poll): fast, fully in-process — resolves branch/remote via go-git, reads a cache, renders a cyan OSC-8 `Trail #N <status>` hyperlink. Never blocks on network.
- **Refresh mode** (`--refresh`, detached): does the authenticated `findTrailByBranch` lookup and rewrites the cache. Spawned via `execx.NonInteractive` (Setsid) and throttled by a lock file.
- Reuses all existing internals: `GetCurrentBranch`, `gitremote.ResolveRemoteRepo`, `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient`, `findTrailByBranch`, `userdirs.Cache()`.

**Verb registration** (`hook_registry.go`, `lifecycle.go`, `hooks.go`) — the `statusline` verb is fast-pathed with its own command and a no-op `PersistentPreRunE`, bypassing the per-invocation logging/perf overhead the other hooks incur (it's polled several times/sec).

**Install/uninstall** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/statusline.go`) — `InstallStatusline` writes the `statusLine` block into `.claude/settings.json`, preserving all other keys. It refuses to overwrite a foreign status line (returns `ErrStatuslineConflict` unless `-f`). `UninstallStatusline` removes only the Entire-owned one and is wired into `UninstallHooks`.

**Opt-in flag** (`setup.go`) — `entire enable [--agent claude-code] --claude-statusline`. On a foreign status line it warns and continues (never fails enable).

### Verification
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint` → 0 issues
- `mise run test` → 6333 tests pass (incl. new `statusline_test.go` + `claude_statusline_test.go`)
- `mise run test:integration` → 370 pass; e2e canary → 4/4 pass
- End-to-end binary smoke test confirmed: install writes the correct block, idempotent re-run, foreign skip + `-f` override, serve renders the hyperlink from cache, and `agent remove` strips both hooks and the status line (while `disable` is a flag-only toggle, consistent with hooks).

One design note worth surfacing for review: the trail web URL is built client-side (`https://entire.io/<forge>/<owner>/<repo>/trails/<n>`) because `api.TrailResource` has no URL field — same approach the original `.mjs` used.

92	// When initLogging is true, it initializes and cleans up hook logging (used by the RunE fallback
93	// since it doesn't go through PersistentPreRunE). Built-in agent subcommands pass false since
94	// their parent command's PersistentPreRunE already handles logging.
95	func executeAgentHook(cmd *cobra.Command, agentName types.AgentName, hookName string, initLogging bool) error {
96		// Skip silently if not in a git repository - hooks shouldn't prevent the agent from working
97		if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(cmd.Context()); err != nil {
98			return nil
99		}
100	
101		// Skip if Entire is not enabled
102		enabled, err := IsEnabled(cmd.Context())
103		if err == nil && !enabled {
104			return nil
105		}
106	
107		if initLogging {
108			cleanup := initHookLogging(cmd.Context())
109			defer cleanup()
110		}
111	
112		// Initialize logging context with agent name
113		ctx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(cmd.Context(), "hooks"), agentName)
114	
115		// Strategy name for logging
116		strategyName := strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit
117	
118		hookType := getHookType(hookName)
119	
120		// Start root perf span — child spans in lifecycle handlers and strategy
121		// methods will automatically nest under this span.
122		ctx, span := perf.Start(ctx, hookName,
123			slog.String("hook_type", hookType))
124		defer span.End()
125	
126		logging.Debug(ctx, "hook invoked",
127			slog.String("hook", hookName),
128			slog.String("hook_type", hookType),
129			slog.String("strategy", strategyName),
130		)
131	
132		// Set the current hook agent so handlers can retrieve it
133		currentHookAgentName = agentName
134		defer func() { currentHookAgentName = "" }()
135	
136		// Use the lifecycle dispatcher for all hooks
137		var hookErr error
138		ag, agentErr := agent.Get(agentName)
139		if agentErr != nil {
140			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent %q: %w", agentName, agentErr)
141		}
142	
143		handler, ok := agent.AsHookSupport(ag)
144		if !ok {
145			return fmt.Errorf("agent %q does not support hooks", agentName)
146		}
147	
148		// Use cmd.InOrStdin() to support testing with cmd.SetIn()
149		event, parseErr := handler.ParseHookEvent(ctx, hookName, cmd.InOrStdin())
150		if parseErr != nil {
151			return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hook event: %w", parseErr)
152		}
153	
154		if event != nil {
155			// Lifecycle event — use the generic dispatcher
156			hookErr = DispatchLifecycleEvent(ctx, ag, event)
157		} else if agentName == agent.AgentNameClaudeCode && hookName == claudecode.HookNamePostTodo {
158			// PostTodo is Claude-specific: creates incremental checkpoints during subagent execution
159			hookErr = handleClaudeCodePostTodo(ctx)
160		}
161		// Other pass-through hooks (nil event, no special handling) are no-ops
162	
163		span.RecordError(hookErr)
164		return hookErr
165	}
166	
167	// newAgentHookVerbCmdWithLogging creates a command for a specific hook verb with structured logging.
168	// It uses the lifecycle dispatcher (ParseHookEvent → DispatchLifecycleEvent) as the primary path.
169	// PostTodo is handled directly as it's Claude-specific and not part of the lifecycle dispatcher.
170	func newAgentHookVerbCmdWithLogging(agentName types.AgentName, hookName string) *cobra.Command {
171		return &cobra.Command{
172			Use:    hookName,
173			Hidden: true,
174			Short:  "Called on " + hookName,
175			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
176				return executeAgentHook(cmd, agentName, hookName, false)
177			},
178		}

## How the Claude Code trail status line works

### Activation (how a user turns it on)

It's **opt-in** and never touches a status line you've already configured. From inside a repo:

```bash
entire enable --agent claude-code --claude-statusline
```

That installs the normal Entire hooks **and** writes a `statusLine` block into `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
"statusLine": {
  "type": "command",
  "command": "entire hooks claude-code statusline",
  "padding": 0
}
```

Behavior around an existing status line:
- **No status line yet** → it's added.
- **You already have one** → Entire refuses to overwrite it, prints `statusLine already configured; skipping — re-run with -f/--force to replace`, and continues. Add `-f`/`--force` to replace it.
- **Re-running** is idempotent (reports "already installed").

You can also pass `--claude-statusline` to a bare `entire enable` (it routes through the agent setup flow). It's removed automatically by `entire agent remove claude-code` (which calls `UninstallHooks`). Note `entire disable` is just an on/off flag toggle — like the hooks, it leaves the status line in `settings.json`.

### What you see

When the current branch has an Entire trail, Claude Code's status bar shows a cyan, clickable **`Trail #42 open`** (an OSC-8 terminal hyperlink to `https://entire.io/gh/<owner>/<repo>/trails/42`). If you're not logged in it shows a dim `Trail: run `entire login``. If there's no trail for the branch, the segment is simply absent.

### How it works under the hood

Claude Code polls the status-line command **several times per second**, so the design (ported from the original Pi `.mjs`) keeps every poll fast and never blocks on the network:

1. **Serve path** (`entire hooks claude-code statusline`, run on every poll): reads Claude Code's session JSON from stdin for the cwd, resolves branch + GitHub remote with in-process go-git (no subprocess, no network), then reads a small cache file under `~/.cache/entire/statusline/<hash>.json`. If a cached result exists it renders it immediately; otherwise it prints nothing.

2. **Background refresh** (detached subprocess, throttled to ~once per 10s when the cache is older than 60s): does the slow part — authenticates and calls the trails API (`findTrailByBranch`) — and rewrites the cache. The link therefore appears/updates a poll later, but the visible command never stalls.

Key implementation points:
- It's a dedicated fast-path command (`newClaudeStatuslineCmd` in `cmd/entire/cli/claude_statusline.go`), registered under `entire hooks claude-code` but **bypassing** the normal hook dispatcher's enabled-checks/perf-spans/per-invocation logging (a no-op `PersistentPreRunE`) since it runs so often.
- It's **native Go** — no Node dependency — and reuses the CLI's existing `GetCurrentBranch`, `gitremote.ResolveRemoteRepo`, `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient`, and `findTrailByBranch`.
- Install/uninstall live in `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/statusline.go`; ownership is detected by the `hooks claude-code statusline` substring in the command, so uninstall only ever removes Entire's own status line and leaves a foreign one intact.

## Summary

Ships the Entire trail status line for Claude Code as a native CLI feature, replacing the standalone Pi `entire-trail-statusline.mjs` script. When the current branch has an Entire trail, Claude Code's status bar shows a clickable, cyan **`Trail #N <status>`** OSC-8 hyperlink to the trail on entire.io.

It's **opt-in** and **no Node dependency** — it reuses the CLI's own trail/auth/git internals.

## How a user activates it

```bash
entire enable --agent claude-code --claude-statusline
```

This writes a `statusLine` block into `.claude/settings.json` pointing at `entire hooks claude-code statusline`. Behavior:

- No status line yet → added.
- Existing status line → **not** clobbered; prints a skip hint. Use `-f`/`--force` to replace.
- Re-running is idempotent. Removed by `entire agent remove claude-code`.

When logged out it renders a dim `Trail: run \`entire login\`` hint; with no trail for the branch the segment is absent.

## How it works

Claude Code polls the status-line command several times per second, so the design keeps every poll fast and non-blocking (ported from the original `.mjs`):

- **Serve path** (every poll): reads the session JSON from stdin, resolves branch + GitHub remote in-process via go-git (no subprocess/network), reads a small cache under `~/.cache/entire/statusline/`, and renders it immediately.
- **Background refresh** (detached, throttled): does the authenticated trail API lookup (`findTrailByBranch`) and rewrites the cache, so the link appears/updates a poll later without ever stalling the visible command.

Implementation notes:

- Dedicated fast-path command (`newClaudeStatuslineCmd`) registered under `entire hooks claude-code` but bypassing the lifecycle dispatcher's enabled-checks / perf-spans / per-invocation logging (no-op `PersistentPreRunE`).
- Reuses `GetCurrentBranch`, `gitremote.ResolveRemoteRepo`, `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient`, `findTrailByBranch`, `userdirs.Cache()`.
- Install/uninstall in `claudecode/statusline.go`; ownership detected by the `hooks claude-code statusline` command substring, so uninstall only removes Entire's own status line and leaves a foreign one intact.
